program_name: Civil and Environmental Engineering (Laurea Magistrale in Ingegneria Civile e Ambientale), University of Brescia — two-year master's degree taught entirely in English
teaching_language: English. UNIBS describes the programme as a two-year Master's Degree Programme taught entirely in English. The degree has a single curriculum, so there is no Italian-taught alternative track within it. An optional 3-CFU unit 'English for Civil and Environmental Engineering' is offered in the first semester as a language-support elective, not as a compensation for the entry requirement.
campus: Brescia — Engineering campus, Department of Civil, Environmental, Architectural Engineering and Mathematics (DICATAM). Educational/teaching services address indicated by UNIBS: Via Branze 38, 25123 Brescia. Student administration (enrolment, fees, transfers, certificates, careers): U.O.C.C. Segreterie Studenti, Via S. Faustino 74/B, 25121 Brescia. [uncertain] — addresses taken from indexed content; note the outline's 'Via Branze 43' does not match the Via Branze 38 figure found.
degree_class: LM-35 — Ingegneria per l'ambiente e il territorio (Environmental Engineering). [uncertain] — Indexed content describes the Brescia 'Civil and environmental engineering / Ingegneria civile e ambientale' master as class LM-35, 2 years, 120 credits, free access. This was NOT read from a live UNIBS page, and it is possible the course is accredited as an inter-class LM-23 & LM-35 degree; it must be re-verified. Note that UNIBS separately runs an Italian-taught 'Ingegneria Civile' LM (LM-23) and an Italian-taught 'Ingegneria per l'ambiente e il territorio' LM — do not conflate them with this English-taught course.
english_delivery_scope: fully_english — The whole degree is delivered in English; UNIBS states the Master's Degree Course in Civil and Environmental Engineering is a two-year Master's Degree Programme taught entirely in English, and that it has a single curriculum. There is therefore no risk of a student being placed in Italian-taught units by curriculum choice, unlike the curriculum-level English offerings at UNIBS (e.g. the Management LM). [uncertain] — free-choice electives and some optional units may still be available only in Italian; this could not be checked.
programme_status: active_first_year — the programme is presented as an active English-taught master's degree recruiting new first-year students, and it appears in the current UNIBS English-taught offer and in the master's pre-assessment procedure for foreign qualifications. No phase-out or suspension notice was found. [uncertain] — activation for AY 2026/2027 specifically could not be confirmed from a live page.
pre_evaluation_required: Yes, for candidates holding a foreign qualification. UNIBS states that for open-access master's degrees in the Economics, Engineering and Law areas — which includes this course — pre-evaluation by the relevant Commission is compulsory for candidates with foreign degrees, to verify curricular and personal preparation requirements. Platform: PICA online procedure, https://www.unibs.it/en/international/degree-seeking-students/admission/pre-evaluation-masters-degrees ; a EUR 20 fee is payable at the end of the procedure. For AY 2026/2027, the first pre-assessment round for non-EU candidates living abroad is open until 15 March 2026 at noon (Italian time), with outcomes emailed around mid-May 2026. EU and EU-equivalent citizens with foreign undergraduate qualifications use a separate, later window (for AY 2025/2026 it ran 30 June – 21 July 2025). [uncertain] — the AY 2026/2027 EU window was not found.
entry_test_name: No standardised or external admission test applies. There is no TOLC, no SAT and no GRE/GMAT requirement for this course: it is an unrestricted-access (accesso libero) engineering master's degree. What replaces a test is an administrative verification of curricular requirements followed by an assessment of the candidate's personal preparation, carried out by the degree-course Commission in the manner set out in the Teaching Regulations (Regolamento didattico) of the study programme. Any assessment that is applied is selective in the sense that it gates admission, but it is not a ranked, competitive entrance exam. [uncertain] — whether the personal-preparation assessment takes the form of an interview, a written test, or a purely documentary review of the transcript could not be verified directly.
admission_type: Open access / unrestricted access (accesso libero, 'corso senza accesso programmato'), subject to verification of curricular requirements and of personal preparation. There is no numerus clausus and no admission ranking. UNIBS lists Civil and Environmental Engineering among the courses without restricted access.
academic_requirements: 1) A three-year bachelor's degree (Italian laurea) or an equivalent foreign qualification recognised as suitable is required. 2) Disciplinary background: applicants should hold a three-year bachelor's degree (or equivalent) in Civil Engineering or in Environmental Engineering, with a sound background in Calculus, Physics, Chemistry, Fluid mechanics and Structural Mechanics. 3) Minimum CFU by sector: graduates of the Italian system under DM 270/04 (or the earlier DM 509/99) may be admitted if they have earned a minimum number of CFU in specific disciplinary areas and scientific-disciplinary sectors (SSD), as detailed in the Academic Regulations of the course. 4) Curricular integrations: any required curricular integrations must be completed BEFORE the assessment of personal preparation takes place — i.e. a candidate cannot be admitted with outstanding curricular debts and make them up during the master's. 5) Personal preparation is then assessed separately. [uncertain] — the exact SSD codes (e.g. ICAR/01, ICAR/02, ICAR/07, ICAR/08, ICAR/09, ING-IND/, MAT/, FIS/, CHIM/) and the per-area minimum CFU figures could not be retrieved, because neither the enrolling page nor the Regolamento didattico PDF could be opened. No minimum bachelor's grade threshold analogous to the Economics-area 85/110 rule was found for this course. [uncertain]
language_requirements: English at CEFR level B2 is required for admission. UNIBS states explicitly that knowledge of English at least at B2 level is required for admission to the master's degree, and that therefore NO credits are reserved for acquiring such skills — i.e. there is no in-programme CFU allocation for English, and the level must already be held. Accepted evidence is expected to follow the standard UNIBS pattern: an international certification at B2 or above from the list recognised by the Language Teaching Centre (Centro Linguistico di Ateneo, CLA), or the CLA UNIBS B2 level certificate (attestazione CLA B2, obtained by passing the CLA level test in the four skills), or a previous degree delivered in English. CLA reference: https://www.unibs.it/en/university/organisation/language-teaching-centre-cla/cla-certification-tests-and-examination-confirmation/attestazione-di-livello-cla-lingua-inglese/attestazione-cla-b2 . A 3-CFU optional unit 'English for Civil and Environmental Engineering' exists in the first semester but is a support elective, not an admission alternative. [uncertain] — the specific list of certificates accepted for THIS course, and the deadline by which the certificate must be produced, could not be verified directly.

Non-EU candidates already legally resident in Italy follow the distinct 'Non-EU candidates living in Italy: master's degrees' route (https://www.unibs.it/en/international/degree-seeking-students/admission/non-eu-candidates-living-italy/non-eu-italy-masters-degrees). required_documents: For the PICA pre-assessment of a foreign qualification: (1) Diploma / degree certificate in the original language; (2) Transcript of records in the original language; both with an official translation into Italian or English unless already issued in one of those languages; (3) Legalisation or Apostille of the diploma and transcript by the competent authorities of the issuing education system; (4) Declaration of Value (Dichiarazione di valore) issued by the competent Italian diplomatic representation in the relevant country, or an equivalent CIMEA comparability statement where accepted; (5) detailed exam syllabi bearing the foreign university's stamp, translated into Italian or English — treated by UNIBS as a preferential/recommended item and particularly important here, because the CFU-per-SSD curricular check depends on being able to map the candidate's courses onto Calculus, Physics, Chemistry, Fluid mechanics and Structural mechanics; (6) proof of English at B2; (7) the EUR 20 pre-assessment fee paid at the end of the PICA procedure; (8) a valid identity document / passport. [uncertain] — no course-specific document list for Civil and Environmental Engineering was found; the list above is the general UNIBS master's pre-assessment set.
entry_exam_or_test: There is no competitive entrance examination. Admission is a two-step verification. Step 1 — curricular requirements: the Commission checks that the applicant holds a suitable bachelor's degree in Civil or Environmental Engineering (or equivalent) and has earned the minimum CFU in the disciplinary areas and SSDs listed in the course Academic Regulations, with an adequate grounding in Calculus, Physics, Chemistry, Fluid mechanics and Structural mechanics. Any curricular integrations must be completed before proceeding. Step 2 — personal preparation: assessed by the Commission in the manner prescribed by the Teaching Regulations of the study programme. For applicants with a foreign qualification both steps are performed inside the PICA pre-assessment procedure, and the applicant receives a written outcome. English B2 must be documented; no CFU are reserved for language acquisition, so it cannot be made up after enrolment. [uncertain] — the concrete form of the personal-preparation assessment (interview vs. documentary review vs. written test), its scheduling and its criteria could not be verified directly.

source_quotes.quote: Knowledge of English at least at B2 level is required for admission to the Master's degree; therefore, no credits are reserved for acquiring such skills.

Students should have a three-year Bachelor's Degree (or equivalent) in Civil Engineering or in Environmental Engineering, with a sound background in Calculus, Physics, Chemistry, Fluid mechanics and Structural Mechanics.

Admission is subject to meeting curricular requirements and an assessment of the candidate's personal preparation. Any required curricular integrations must be completed before the evaluation of personal preparation.

Graduates from the Italian system under DM 270/04 or the previous DM 509/99 can be admitted if they have earned a minimum number of CFU in specific disciplinary areas and scientific-disciplinary sectors (SSD), as detailed in the course's Academic Regulations.

The course is organised over two academic years and foresees the acquisition of a total of 120 credits divided among specific subjects, related and additional subjects chosen by the student, as well as final examination preparation activities.
The Master's Degree in Civil and Environmental Engineering has a single curriculum.
Civil and Environmental Engineering is listed as a course without restricted access.

The programme has a duration of 2 years with 120 credits, is located in Brescia, and has free access; an optional course in 'English for Civil and Environmental Engineering' worth 3 credits is offered in the first semester.
The pre-assessment procedure for non-EU holders of foreign degrees aiming to enroll in Italian or English taught postgraduate degrees for 2026/2027 a.y. is open till 15 March 2026.

For open access master's degrees in Economics, Engineering and Law areas, pre-evaluation by the relevant Commission is compulsory for candidates with foreign degrees to verify if they meet specific curricular and personal preparation requirements.
The admission procedure for Master's Degree programs in Engineering will be open from July 1 to September 30, 2025.
